page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.large is a compute-optimized server instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz, delivering 2 virtual CPUs mapped to 1 physical core via Hyper-Threading with dedicated CPU allocation on a KVM hypervisor. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of RAM, corresponding to 2.0 GB per vCPU, alongside a 48 MB L3 cache. Supported hardware features include AVX, AVX-512 (f and vnni), AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets. The instance includes no local storage or attached GPU accelerators and relies on a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark results demonstrate moderate single-thread compute capabilities balanced against limited multi-core throughput. The instance scored 1487.0 on single-core Geekbench and 1874.59 on single-core stress-ng tests, placing single-thread performance in the average benchmark tier. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 27.47 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core stress-ng (1926.09) and multi-core Geekbench (1742.0) scores rank in the lower performance brackets due to the two-vCPU core count limit. Uncached memory read bandwidth measured 14.32 GB/sec. For application benchmarks, Redis SET operations reached 1.91 million operations per second and static web serving throughput measured 3.33 GB/sec.

From an engineering perspective, ecs.c7.large provides a low-capacity compute footprint suited for small-scale background execution. Its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio prioritizes execution core allocation over large memory allocation, creating a resource bottleneck for memory-intensive applications or heavy parallel workloads. The configuration is optimal for lightweight web servers, microservice backends, entry-level API gateways, and single-threaded execution tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.large is an entry-level compute-optimized instance built on an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz within a KVM hypervisor. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs across 1 physical core, 4.0 GB of RAM, 48 MB of L3 cache, and instruction support including AVX-512 VNNI and AES. The instance features a 2 Gbps network baseline with zero local storage and no GPU accelerators. In benchmarks, single-threaded performance performs in the average range with a single-core Geekbench score of 1487.0, whereas multi-core execution and memory bandwidth fall into lower performance tiers due to the low thread and memory count. Redis SET operations achieve 1.91 million operations per second and static web throughput reaches 3.33 GB/sec. This configuration offers an entry-level dedicated compute profile suited for light web serving, basic background tasks, and low-concurrency microservices.
